chapter: Young players, schools and studio work
title: Hinton at CBS in jeans and Percy Faith's dark suit
summary: Hinton is told to wear a dark suit on the Percy Faith radio show.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Right, I agree. I can remember being the recipient of that once. I -- for so long I had been working with all of you guys in the studios, recording studios where we came in sneakers and jeans because we were in a recording studio. And I remember once I got a call for a radio show, which was -- you know, there wouldn't be no audience there, just a radio show in a studio. And of course I went just like I went to the recording session. And I remember it was at CBS, and I think the big detail, when I went there and the contractor, Lou Shobe Shubey's stickler for punctuality and cleanliness and everything that was good for musicians. And I walked in with my bass, and had on some jeans and very loud leather jacket, and here was a big orchestra, 50 men, Percy Faith's orchestra. And down he came and I was there, and I made the downbeat, and he sidled over to me and says, don't you have a dark suit? but And I said, yes, I have a dark suit, / I thought a radio show in a studio -- we have dark suits. And I felt terribly appreciated, but I appreciated him pulling my coat, as we say, because it taught me when you
go, as you say, when you're going in that part of town in that particular society, then you act like that.

Yeah, when you're in Rome, you do what the Romans tell you to do. I know, that was dark suit, black Standard words. ties. / There were even jokes about it. I've got two dark suits and two black ties and that's going to have to last me until I die. You know, there was a time when I think -- even these were days when people wore suits and ties, I don't think I had anything but dark suits and dark ties, even when I'd go out I'd wear them.
